seoTitle: TradingView Discount: How to Get 15% Off in Feb 2026
metaDescription: Learn where to find official TradingView discount codes, how to apply a 15% off promo, which plans qualify, and how to avoid expired offers.
intro: Subscribing to TradingView's Pro, Pro+, or Premium plans can get expensive over time, so grabbing a legitimate discount is worth the extra few minutes of research. This guide covers where TradingView's own referral and promotional offers actually show up, how to confirm a 15% off deal applies to your chosen plan, and how to avoid the frustration of trying to redeem a code that's already expired. It's aimed at anyone who wants premium charting features without paying full price for them.

steps.heading: Recognize TradingView's referral offer when you land on it
steps.body: TradingView runs an ongoing referral program, and if you arrive at tradingview.com through a referral or affiliate link, you'll often see a popup confirming it — something like "You were invited to TradingView," explaining that joining through that link unlocks a reward once you purchase your first subscription. This is one of the most reliable ways a 15% or dollar-value discount actually gets applied, because it's tracked automatically by the link itself rather than requiring you to type a code in later.

image.caption: TradingView's referral landing popup, confirming the visit came through an invite link and explaining the reward tied to a first subscription purchase.

steps.heading: Check your inbox for official TradingView promotions
steps.body: TradingView also emails subscribers directly about seasonal sales and plan promotions if you've signed up for their mailing list. Searching your inbox for terms like "tradingview promo" or "tradingview discount" surfaces these official messages, which is a safer way to confirm an offer is real compared to trusting a code posted somewhere off-platform. Official emails come from TradingView's own domain and link back to tradingview.com directly, rather than through a third party.

image.caption: An official TradingView email located via inbox search, with the sender and unsubscribe link both pointing back to tradingview.com.

steps.heading: Apply the code or link at checkout
steps.body: Whether you're using a referral link or a promo code from an email, the discount typically applies automatically once you're in TradingView's checkout flow for a Pro, Pro+, or Premium plan — either the referral tracking carries through from the link you clicked, or there's a promo code field to enter during payment. Complete the plan selection first, since the discount is usually tied to your first paid subscription rather than an upgrade or renewal.

steps.heading: Confirm which plans the discount actually covers
steps.body: Not every promotion applies uniformly across TradingView's tiers. A referral reward or seasonal discount might only reduce the cost of Pro, or it might apply across Pro, Pro+, and Premium — this varies by offer, so check the terms shown on the referral page or in the promotional email before assuming your preferred plan qualifies. If the discount doesn't show up as expected during checkout, that's usually the reason.

steps.heading: Watch for expired or invalid codes
steps.body: Seasonal promo codes shared around Black Friday or Cyber Monday tend to have hard cutoff dates, and codes that circulate on blogs or forums after that window closes simply won't work anymore. If a code fails at checkout, don't assume you mistyped it — check the date it was originally published first, since an expired code is by far the most common reason a discount doesn't apply.

steps.heading: Treat third-party promo codes with some caution
steps.body: Codes shared by individual creators or affiliate sites are usually legitimate extensions of TradingView's official referral program, but they're still worth double-checking against TradingView's own site before you commit to a plan around one. If a deal looks unusually large or asks you to do anything outside TradingView's normal checkout, that's a sign to stick with the official referral or in-app promotion instead.

faq.question: Is the 15% off TradingView promo code always available?
faq.answer: Promo codes and referral rewards are typically time-limited or tied to specific campaigns, so availability changes — check the current offer directly on TradingView's site or through an official email before assuming it still applies.

faq.question: Can I stack multiple discount codes together?
faq.answer: Most platforms, including TradingView, generally don't allow stacking multiple promo codes on a single purchase, so check the terms of any offer before assuming you can combine them.

faq.question: Does the discount apply to all subscription plans?
faq.answer: Eligibility varies by promotion — some cover only Pro, while others extend to Pro+ and Premium, so confirm before checking out.

faq.question: What happens if my promo code doesn't work at checkout?
faq.answer: This usually means the code has expired or doesn't apply to your selected plan, so double-check both before trying again with a fresh, currently-valid offer.

faq.question: How do I know a TradingView discount offer is legitimate?
faq.answer: Official offers come through tradingview.com itself or emails from TradingView's own domain. If a referral link takes you to TradingView's site and shows a confirmation popup naming the reward, that's a genuine tracked offer.
